correctness.rationale: The exact 2x2 Laurent symbol B=[[y,1],[1,y^2]] follows directly from GP(n,2), and det B=z^{-3}Phi3 Phi5. At Phi3, B^2=Phi3 times an invertible local matrix, the mod-Phi3 rank is one and the entire 2e-dimensional F4 component is a single zero Jordan block. At Phi5, trace is a unit, determinant valuation one, and a Hensel splitting yields one length-e zero block per F16 residue root. All other components are invertible. This proves the complete kernel and first-entry counts for arbitrary n. The fixed-point count follows from the Smith invariants of B+I, and the all-return-time expression follows from polynomial Smith invariants. Independently, supplied exact scripts checked 771 finite kernel cases, 87040 individual states, 832 return-time matrix/Smith comparisons and 396 fixed-point exponents. Finite tests are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: GP(n,2) is a natural cubic infinite graph family including the Petersen and Dürer graphs. The complete first-periodic-entry census depends on two distinct cyclotomic resonances, 3 and 5, and the dyadic multiplicity, while the precise nilpotent Jordan blocks have unequal lengths 2e versus e. This produces an exact all-n arithmetic phase diagram, a sharp transient time, and a reproducible return-time census, rather than a narrow arbitrary numerical slice or a routine new example. It distinguishes dynamics not detected by real graph spectra.
